newsitem.title: USA: Heinz's O'Reilly sees further 96 eps growth.
newsitem.headline: Heinz's O'Reilly sees further 96 eps growth.

text.p: H.J. Heinz Co. Chairman and Chief Executive Tony O'Reilly said on Tuesday he expected earnings to grow over the rest of the fiscal year, although the company's goal of reducing end-of-quarter sales loads affected the quarter.

"I am pleased by the improvement in our operating performance and market share and fully expect earnings to continue to gain momentum through the fiscal year towards our double digit goal," O'Reilly said in a statement.
But O'Reilly said the company's policy of reducing high-cost end-of-quarter sales loads affected results.

This practice involves a short-term reduction in sales for some of the company's products but results in better returns on capital and greater efficiencies in the medium and long-term, Heinz said in a statement.
During the first quarter, the policy resulted in some volume declines, particularly in retail frozen potatoes and infant food overseas, Heinz said.
But core products such as Heinz ketcup, pet food, tuna and single-serve condiments showed strong growth, Heinz said.

"As expected, our commitment to reducing high-cost end-of-quarter sales loads has affected our current quarter," O'Reilly said. "This strategy will, when fully implemented, enable Heinz to enjoy reduced working capital and production costs."
Heinz on Tuesday said its first quarter 1996 earnings were $0.48 per share against $0.46 per share last year.
Year-on-year comparisons of results benefited from acquisitions in four of the company's six core categories: pet food, infant foods, foodservice and tuna.

Results were also affected by divestitures of non-strategic businesses including an overseas mushroom business, Weight Watchers Magazine, an overseas sweetener business, a powdered beverage business in South America and two regional dry pet food product lines.

Acquisitions affecting result comparisons were pet food companies Nature's Recipe Pet Food in the United States and Alimentos Pilar S.A. in Argentina, infant food companies Fattoria Scaldasole S.p.A. in Italy and Earth's Best Inc. in the United States, food service companies Southern Country Foods Ltd. in Australia, Britwest Ltd. in the United Kingdom and Craig's foodservice business in New Zealand, and tuna companies Indian Ocean Tuna Ltd. in the Seychelles and the Mareblu brand of canned tuna in Italy.
